blocks.text: An FDPS revision is released only after a C pass and with every Action from reviews A, B and C closed and accepted, and with no Non-compliant Compliance Statement over its range.

Release gate. An FDPS revision shall only be submitted to the release lifecycle once the FDPS has passed a C (Detail) review, carried forward where 6C.12 allows, and every Action raised at any A, B or C review covering the FDPS, including re-reviews and Actions raised from conditions of agreement (6C.19, 6C.22), is closed, and every Compliance Statement of the FDPS over the revision's effectivity range is Compliant or an approved Not applicable (6A.17). A Cancelled Action shall count as closed only with a reason and the approval of the review chair. While PLM issues releases (6A.13), the PLM release workflow shall obtain the Hub's confirmation that the gate is met before releasing, through the documented interface (2J.2); a release without that confirmation shall be flagged as a discrepancy.

Carry-forward and re-review. A later design change shall invalidate a review only if it is substantial (6C.17). A passed C review shall carry forward to later revisions of the FDPS unless the Design Authority for the area judges a change since the review snapshot to be substantial. The Design Authority shall assess every change against the snapshot when approving the FDPS revision for release, and the carry-forward shall be recorded with that assessment (assessor, date and reasons). If a change is judged substantial, a re-review shall be held at the FDPS's current review stage (normally C), scoped to the affected FDPS and the changed areas. At a re-review, the agreements required (6C.19, 6C.22) are those of the Disciplines and interfacing Systems whose areas the change affects, as identified by the Design Authority; the other agreements are carried forward from the review it follows and recorded as carried forward. The re-review's snapshot then becomes the reference for later assessments.

Approval of non-applicability. A recorded non-applicability of an inherited Requirement (6B.7) shall be approved by a Design Lead whose delegated area (6C.14) covers every Sub-system through which the Requirement reaches the FDPS. A recorded non-applicability of a TSM (6B.7, 6B.11) shall be approved by a Design Authority whose area covers the FDPS's owning Design Team, or a Design Type through which the TSM reaches the FDPS.

Roles. The Technical Authority for Design (also known as the Design Licence Holder) is responsible for the design and gives the Pass or Fail at each review. The Technical Authority for Design may delegate release authority to Design Leads, Design Approvers or Design Authorities, who approve FDPSs and parts for release within their area. There is no FDPS Design Lead role: breaks of an FDPS's inherited interfaces are approved by a Design Lead whose area is the FDPS's lead Sub-system (1.7.7), which for a Sub-structure FDPS is its lead Sub-structure (6C.21). Each Production Hub shall hold a Role register recording, for each person, each role held (Annex B.4: Technical Authority for Design, Design Authority, Design Lead, Design Approver, Discipline Lead), the delegated authority it carries, the area it covers (for example a Sub-system or Sub-structure, System, Design Sub-team, Design Team, Design Type or Discipline), who delegated it, and its validity dates. The software shall check every approval, agreement, release and decision against the Role register at the date it is given.

Substantial change. A change shall be substantial if, judged against the review snapshot (6C.9), it adversely affects compliance with any Requirement or TSM, degrades form, fit or function, degrades an interface, or adds a new interface with another System. A change that improves or restores compliance does not adversely affect it. A reduced margin that remains compliant shall not count as adversely affecting compliance, but the margin change shall be recorded. Added Part Instances or interfaces shall be substantial only if they add a new interface with another System or adversely affect compliance with a Requirement or TSM. A change that is not substantial shall not require a new review, but shall be recorded against the affected FDPS, with its author, date and reason, and linked to the review it follows. A Change Record may carry several change types, and the substantial assessment shall be recorded for each affected FDPS.

Non-compliance and release. Concessions are part of the manufacturing standard, not the design standard, and Concession records are not in the current scope (section 7). A known non-compliance of the design with a Requirement or TSM shall be recorded as a Compliance Statement with position Non-compliant over the effectivity range concerned, linked to the Issue that records it (2E). No FDPS revision shall be released for any effectivity at which a Compliance Statement of the FDPS is Non-compliant (6C.11). Where a non-compliance is found after a revision has been released, that released revision and its baselines shall stay unchanged as the as-designed record of the effectivities built to it; the Non-compliant statement shall be shown at those effectivities in every view and report (5.17, 2.8), and release for those effectivities shall stay blocked until a Compliance Statement restores compliance. How a built aircraft is recovered or accepted is outside the software until section 7 is in scope.
